reason: The finding is text-only and post-deadline, so it cannot hurt the finals (0 GPU, 0 slots, R1-R10 untouched). It also adds nothing on private (value 0). It is refuted as specified for two reasons. (1) It is mostly a duplicate. The same scan's R14L-3 text for s3.11 already says '(1) Separate FINALS rules from EXPLORATION rules' and '(2) Every ban gets an expiry and a named re-open trigger', and it gives the same three triggers as examples. The rewritten s3.7 (ceiling-first) already covers the meter for 'agent-rounds on families whose oracle ceiling < bar'. The only new parts are the field names PURPOSE and COST METER, and the retro-test. (2) The retro-test cannot fail, so it tests nothing. T3 fires by construction: the Kaggle GPU quota reset at 26 Sep 00:00Z (CONTEXT l.1252, l.1545, l.1824). On 25 Sep ~19/30 h were used ('11 h left before the reset', l.1816), then usage dropped to 0 at the reset, and it was 07:55/30 at 21:5xZ (l.2542). So 'idle > 50% with >= 3 days left' becomes true at every weekly reset, including 26 Sep 00:00Z, which is before the 12:00Z cutoff. T2 fires every day. At 25 Sep 22:16Z at least 5 teams had already jumped +0.003 or more (syed3000 0.953->0.965, LIN mimosa ->0.962, Mositaku ->0.958, Alfonso 0.948->0.957, Miz 0.954->0.957, plus several 0.953/0.954->0.955/0.956; round3/report.json new_facts (2)). CONTEXT l.2131/l.2140 records these post-reset bursts as 'the daily pattern, not a signal'. That is why E10 P2 already needs an identical score >= 0.956. Whether T1 fired depends on wording. Round 3 found 'no public notebook scores above 0.953' at 22:16-22:43Z 25 Sep. y3uanm's public notebooks never trained and have no public weights ('C10 cannot fire', IDEAS.md I-119). So 'T1 fired at 25 Sep 22:23Z' holds only if the trigger is worded now, after the fact. The triggers were fitted to events already seen (T2 'seen 26 Sep 20:01Z', T3 'true at 21:5xZ'), and the decision rule makes 'supported' the outcome whatever the log shows. The rule also checks only whether a trigger fired, not whether re-opening would have been worth it. The retrain prior was E[public] ~0 (-0.003..+0.002) and our model-swap record is 0/5. A trigger that fires at every quota reset or overnight burst is the same as having no ban. So the retro-test cannot decide the wording of s3.11 or show that s3.11 needs a correction.
fix: Post-deadline and text only. Do not add a separate item 12. Merge into s3.11 (2) one sentence: 'Write each rule with PURPOSE (public overfit / in-sample lab / runtime / post-hoc), SCOPE (finals vs exploration), EXPIRY and RE-OPEN TRIGGER, and log a daily COST METER (GPU-h that will expire unused before the next reset, slots left unused, rounds spent on families below the ceiling bar).' Drop the retro-test as written. If a retro-test is kept, each trigger must fire rarely: (a) count how many intel windows between 20 and 29 Sep each trigger fires in, using round*/scan_browser + e10_watch; a trigger that fires in more than 1 window in 3 is rejected. (b) Redefine T3 as 'projected unused quota at the NEXT reset > 50%', not '% idle', which is 100% at every reset. (c) Word T1 against a public notebook's own displayed score and public weights, as in E10 P3, so that R3S-6/y3uanm does not count. (d) Say openly that the test cannot measure whether re-opening would have been worth it: exp71 was never trained, and the retrain priors were ~0.
realistic_gain: 0 on public and private, and no finals effect. For the next competition it at most saves a sentence of duplicated lessons text. The retro-test as written costs ~1 eng-h and gives a result that is decided in advance ('supported'), so its information gain is ~0. Merged into s3.11, the template fields are a small but real improvement to process hygiene.
